\chapter{Complexity — Composition}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Composition
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This module provides the basic computability combinators for bundled multi-tape
Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet: the identity function, every constant
function, and equality testing against a fixed word are computable in linear
time, and time-bounded computability is closed under sequential composition.
It also provides two untimed guarded combinators: sequential composition of two
arbitrary machines at the level of their halting relations, and branching
between two machines according to a predicate decided by a third machine.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[The one-state copy machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.idTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.idTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
The machine over the Boolean alphabet with no work tapes and a single state
that copies its input to its output: on scanning an input symbol it appends
that symbol to the output and moves the input head one cell right, and on
scanning a boundary blank it halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Run invariant of the copy machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.idTM_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.idTM_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.idTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word and run the one-state copy machine from its initial
configuration on input $x$.  For every $t \le \abs{x}$, after $t$ steps the
machine is still live in its unique state, its input head sits at position
$t + 1$ (in the convention where position $0$ is the left boundary blank and
position $j$ with $1 \le j \le \abs{x}$ scans the $j$-th input symbol), and its
output is exactly the first $t$ symbols of $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Identity is linear-time computable]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_id}
\label{Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_id}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.idTM, Turing.FinTM.idTM_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
There exist a multi-tape Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a
constant $c$ such that $M$ computes the identity function on Boolean words in
time $c \cdot (n + 1)$: on every input $x$, within $c \cdot (\abs{x} + 1)$
steps $M$ halts with output exactly $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The constant-word emission machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.constTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.constTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.emitAction}
For a fixed Boolean word $w$, the machine over the Boolean alphabet with no
work tapes whose states are $\{0, \dots, \abs{w}\}$, forming the emission chain
for $w$: state $i < \abs{w}$, regardless of the symbols scanned, appends the
$i$-th symbol of $w$ (zero-indexed) to the output and passes to state $i + 1$,
and state $\abs{w}$ halts.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{3}
For every fixed Boolean word $w$ there exist a multi-tape Turing machine $M$

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The fixed-word comparator machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.emitAction}
For fixed Boolean words $w_0$, $u$, $v$, the machine over the Boolean alphabet
with no work tapes whose states are $\abs{w_0} + 1$ comparison states together
with an emission chain for $u$ and an emission chain for $v$.  Comparison state
$i < \abs{w_0}$ moves the input head right and passes to comparison state
$i + 1$ when the scanned symbol is the $i$-th symbol of $w_0$, and enters the
emission chain for $v$ otherwise; comparison state $\abs{w_0}$ enters the
chain for $u$ on a boundary blank and the chain for $v$ on any remaining
symbol.  Each emission chain writes its word one symbol per step and halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Emission phase of the comparator]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ifEq_finish}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ifEq_finish}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.emit_halts, Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Fix Boolean words $w_0$, $u$, $v$, an input word $x$, and a Boolean $b$, and
write $z$ for the word $u$ if $b$ is true and $v$ if $b$ is false.  Let $c$ be
any configuration of the fixed-word comparator machine for $w_0$, $u$, $v$ on
input $x$ whose state is the initial state of the emission chain for $z$ and
whose output is still empty.  Then after exactly $\abs{z} + 1$ further steps
the machine has halted with output exactly $z$, independently of the position
of the input head in $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparison invariant of the comparator]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.ifEq_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.ifEq_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.ifEqTM, Turing.FinTM.ifEq_finish, Turing.FinTM.inputSymbol_at, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right}
\difficulty{5}
Fix Boolean words $w_0$, $u$, $v$ and an input word $x$, and let $i$ and $r$ be
natural numbers with $\abs{w_0} = i + r$, $i \le \abs{x}$, and the first $i$
symbols of $x$ equal to the first $i$ symbols of $w_0$.  From any configuration
of the fixed-word comparator machine for $w_0$, $u$, $v$ on input $x$ that is
in comparison state $i$ with its input head at position $i + 1$ (position $0$
being the left boundary blank) and with empty output, there is a
$t \le r + \max(\abs{u}, \abs{v}) + 2$ such that after $t$ steps the machine
has halted, with output $u$ if $x = w_0$ and output $v$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Composition of time-bounded computations]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp}
\label{Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_comp}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedComp_start, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet,
let $f$ and $g$ be functions on Boolean words, and let $T_1, T_2 : \mathbb{N}
\to \mathbb{N}$ with $T_2$ monotone.  Suppose $M_1$ computes $f$ in time $T_1$
and $M_2$ computes $g$ in time $T_2$, meaning that on every input $x$ the
machine halts within $T_i(\abs{x})$ steps with the function value on its
output tape.  Then there exist a machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes the composite $g \circ f$ in time
$n \mapsto c \cdot \bigl(T_1(n) + T_2(T_1(n)) + 1\bigr)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Partial sequential composition]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_partial}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_comp_partial}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedComp_start, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_init, Turing.FinTM.bufferedFirstCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
For any two multi-tape Turing machines $M_1$ and $M_2$ over the Boolean
alphabet — with no totality or time hypotheses — there exists a machine $M$
such that for all Boolean words $x$ and $w$: $M$ halts on input $x$ with
output $w$ (within some number of steps) if and only if there is a Boolean
word $y$ such that $M_1$ halts on input $x$ with output $y$ and $M_2$ halts on
input $y$ with output $w$.  In particular, if $M_1$ diverges on $x$, or halts
but $M_2$ diverges on its output, then $M$ diverges on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The conditional-dispatch machine]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.condTM}
\label{Turing.FinTM.condTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.branchTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.rightAction}
Given three machines $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ over the Boolean alphabet with $k_D$,
$k_1$, $k_2$ work tapes respectively, the machine with $k_D + k_1 + k_2$ work
tapes whose finite control simulates $D$ on the first tape block with $D$'s
emissions suppressed and the first emitted symbol captured in a state
register.  After the simulated $D$ halts, a control phase rewinds the input
head to its initial position and then transfers control to a disjoint copy of
the branch union of $M_1$ and $M_2$ selected by the register bit, running on
the fresh remaining tape blocks; when the register is empty at dispatch the
machine halts.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding of a controller configuration]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.controlCfg}
\label{Turing.FinTM.controlCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.condTM}
Given machines $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ over the Boolean alphabet and a configuration
$c$ of $D$ on an input $x$, the configuration of the conditional-dispatch
machine for $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ on $x$ whose control state pairs the state of
$c$ with the first symbol (if any) of $c$'s output stored in the register,
whose input head agrees with that of $c$, whose first tape block carries $c$'s
work tapes while all branch tapes are blank with heads at the origin, and
whose real output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One-step lockstep of the embedded controller]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.controlCfg_step}
\label{Turing.FinTM.controlCfg_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.condTM, Turing.FinTM.controlCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet and let $c$ be a
configuration of $D$ on an input $x$ whose state is not the halting state.
Then one step of the conditional-dispatch machine from the embedded controller
configuration of $c$ equals the embedded controller configuration of one step
of $D$ from $c$; in particular the register tracks the first symbol of the
simulated output, with no hypothesis on $c$'s output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Controller lockstep through the first halt]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.controlCfg_run}
\label{Turing.FinTM.controlCfg_run}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.condTM, Turing.FinTM.controlCfg, Turing.FinTM.controlCfg_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{3}
Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be a
configuration of $D$ on an input $x$, and let $t$ be a number of steps such
that the run of $D$ from $c$ has not halted at any time $s < t$.  Then the
$t$-step run of the conditional-dispatch machine from the embedded controller
configuration of $c$ equals the embedded controller configuration of the
$t$-step run of $D$ from $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Reaching the selected branch start]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.condTM_start}
\label{Turing.FinTM.condTM_start}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.output_unique, Turing.FinTM.branchTM, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.condTM, Turing.FinTM.controlCfg, Turing.FinTM.controlCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.rewind_from_any, Turing.FinTM.rightCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a
Boolean word, and let $b$ be a Boolean such that $D$ halts on input $x$ with
the singleton output consisting of $b$ alone (within some number of steps).
Then there exist a time $t$ and residual contents and head positions for the
controller's tape block such that the $t$-step run of the conditional-dispatch
machine from its initial configuration on $x$ is exactly the right-block
embedding of the initial configuration on $x$ of the branch machine selected
by $b$ (the branch union of $M_1$ and $M_2$), alongside those residual
controller tapes.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Branching on a decided predicate]
\lean{Turing.FinTM.exists_cond}
\label{Turing.FinTM.exists_cond}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.Computes, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.branchTM, Turing.FinTM.branchTM_computes, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.condTM, Turing.FinTM.condTM_start, Turing.FinTM.rightCfg, Turing.FinTM.rightCfg_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $D$, $M_1$, $M_2$ be multi-tape Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet
and let $p$ be a Boolean-valued predicate on Boolean words such that $D$
computes the function $x \mapsto [p(x)]$: on every input $x$ it eventually
halts with the single symbol $p(x)$ as its output.  Then there exists a
machine $M$ such that for all Boolean words $x$ and $w$: $M$ halts on input
$x$ with output $w$ (within some number of steps) if and only if the branch
machine selected by $p(x)$ — namely $M_1$ when $p(x)$ is true and $M_2$ when
$p(x)$ is false — halts on that same input $x$ with output $w$ (within some
number of steps).
\end{theorem}
